title: Everyone is talking about Albanese’s selfie with Trump. What was the PM thinking? | Tom McIlroy
content:
Trump is not popular in Australia, even if the prime minister views close ties with the US as a key pillar of foreign policy

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

    • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

    • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

    When Anthony Albanese arrived at the United Nations general assembly in September last year, he was desperate for face time with Donald Trump.

    The prime minister had been due to hold his first meeting with the US president on the sidelines of the G7 summit in Canada that June, but Trump cancelled at the last minute. By September, he was under pressure to lock in Trump’s support for the Aukus nuclear submarine agreement and show Australia remained a top tier ally.

title: Defiance, threats and a ‘rebirth’: five key points from day two of the UN’s big gathering
content:
Iran took a combative tone, a new Venezuela is announced, and Ukraine’s president aims at the Kremlin’s coffers

The rubber hit the road this week at the UN general assembly at a time of global urgency, with the Middle East crisis reverberating through markets around the world, AI sparking existential concerns, and few signs of cooperation between the US and China in their great power rivalry.

World leaders have gathered in New York to make their feelings known, both at the podium and at crucial meetings on the sidelines. Amid the chaos of the politicking and background briefings, here is a selection of key points we saw on day two.

title: UK shares findings of damning climate crisis national security report suppressed under Starmer
content:
El Niño poses critical threat to nations’ defences, says Ed Miliband in presentation to global foreign ministers

The UK has warned countries around the world that the climate and nature crises and the coming El Niño threaten their national security and defence, presenting foreign ministries with the findings of an explosive report suppressed under Keir Starmer.

Ed Miliband, the UK’s foreign secretary, made a presentation to the foreign ministers of the EU as well as Kenya and other countries on Wednesday night at a private meeting during the UN general assembly in New York, based on the report by the UK’s spy chiefs that found the collapse of natural systems around the world would lead to conflict, migration and food shortages.
snippet: El Niño poses critical threat to nations’ defences, says Ed Miliband in presentation to global foreign ministers

title: OpenAI’s Altman and Anthropic’s Amodei address UN security council
content:
Heads of two of the world’s largest artificial intelligence companies give separate briefings on AI safety

Sam Altman of OpenAI and Dario Amodei of Anthropic, heads of two of the world’s largest artificial intelligence companies, addressed the United Nations security council on Wednesday in separate briefings on AI safety.

“We have a choice in front of us,” Altman told the council. “AI can either be more like a new renaissance of creativity and discovery, or more like a new industrial revolution of upheaval and disarray.”

title: Milei threatens at UN that Argentina will take ‘matters into our own hands’ on Falklands
content:
Argentinian president accuses United Nations of being filled with ‘parasites’ in bellicose general assembly speech

Javier Milei has condemned the UN as he warned that Argentina would take “matters into our own hands” in its dispute with Britain over the sovereignty of the Falkland Islands.

In a caustic speech at the general assembly in New York, the Argentinian president criticised the UN for being ineffective when it came to the long-running tensions over the British overseas territory in the south Atlantic known in Argentina as the Malvinas.

title: ‘We hope he’ll accept’: US invites Putin to G20 summit at Trump golf club
content:
Kremlin yet to respond publicly to US invitation that is likely to raise concerns from Ukraine and EU countries

The United States has invited Vladimir Putin to take part in the meeting of the G20 scheduled in Miami in December in what would be the first major summit with the Russian leader present since he launched his invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

The invitation, which marks a significant reversal by the Trump administration of Russia’s international isolation, was announced by Marco Rubio, the US secretary of state, during a press conference on the sidelines of the United Nations conference in New York.

title: The Guardian view on the future of the UN: more embattled, but more necessary, than ever | Editorial
content:
As the secretary general, António Guterres, prepares to step down, the general assembly is highlighting the scale of the organisation’s challenges

The United Nations was created, its charter states, to “save succeeding generations from the scourge of war”. Donald Trump used his address to the general assembly to threaten Iran, another member state, with annihilation again. The charter also speaks of the obligations of international law. On Venezuela, Mr Trump gloated that “to the victor belong the spoils”. His speech in New York on Tuesday might be regarded as an improvement on last year’s only in that it was not an explicit, full-scale attack on the UN itself, merely on its founding principles.
snippet: As the secretary general, António Guterres, prepares to step down, the general assembly is highlighting the scale of the organisation’s challenges

title: Iran’s president hits out at ‘bully’ Trump in UN speech but signals willingness to talk
content:
Masoud Pezeshkian says Tehran is ready for dialogue and diplomacy ‘but without the language of force’

Iran’s president, Masoud Pezeshkian, turned the tables on Donald Trump, describing the US as the true bully and terrorist in the Middle East while insisting that Iran had always shown a commitment to the negotiating table.

In a defiant speech to the UN general assembly in New York, his first since the US and Israel launched an all-out war on Iran, Pezeshkian repeatedly vowed that Tehran would never bend the knee to the US.

title: UK politics: PM’s new anti-disinformation unit gets cross-party backing, as Farage declares it an attack on free speech – as it happened
content:
Farage referred to the new unit and said Burnham was setting it up ‘using the excuse that Russia wants to interfere with elections’

The former Labour minister leading the government’s review into youth unemployment has written to 100 firms to ask them to provide work placements and jobs for young people, the Press Association reports. PA says:

Alan Milburn, who was commissioned by former prime minister Keir Starmer to lead the government’s review into worklessness, has approached “business leaders” in sectors including rail, transport and utilities to ask them to provide more chances for young people.

The Milburn review said Royal Mail, Octopus Energy, Greene King and Lloyds bank are among the companies who are already offering opportunities to school and university leavers. They are taking part in the review’s First Chance scheme, which has come from the review.

title: Trump’s UN speech was delusional and dangerous | Kenneth Roth
content:
It is sad and dangerous that at such a perilous moment, the United States is saddled with a president like Trump

Donald Trump’s speech on Tuesday to the United Nations general assembly was an object lesson in his lawless rule and remarkable capacity for self-delusion. Disregarding the UN charter’s emphasis on the peaceful resolution of disputes, he doubled down on his violent unilateralism while denigrating the global issues that the UN is designed to address.

For many, the headline remark was his musing about whether to “annihilate the Islamic Republic” of Iran. “Do I drive them into hell with no chance of survival and no hope of future greatness or generations?”

Kenneth Roth is a Guardian US columnist, a senior fellow at Yale University and a former executive director of Human Rights Watch. He is the author of Righting Wrongs: Three Decades on the Front Lines Battling Abusive Governments

title: Burnham survived his first Trump meeting. His nice hair may have had something to do with it | Emma Brockes
content:
The PM’s shiny newness could explain the easy ride he got this time. But who would dare predict the ever-shifting weather in the president’s head?

Watching footage of Andy Burnham at the UN general assembly on Tuesday was like watching your child from behind a tree in the playground. Are they making friends? How normal do they seem relative to the average? How will they react when they come into contact with that hulking great child who seems to be running things? Burnham’s first face-to-face with Donald Trump was billed as a knife-edge encounter that, due to the latter’s capriciousness, could go either way. In the event, it was drama-free, leaving observers to ask: was it Burnham’s brilliance or simply the weather in Trump’s head?

title: Iran denies dropping preconditions amid ‘very productive’ three-hour UN talks in New York
content:
Trump says further talks possible as barrel of Brent crude falls to below $100 for first time in two weeks

  • United Nations general assembly – latest updates

    • United Nations general assembly – latest updates

    Iran has pushed back on claims that it dropped former preconditions for reopening the strait of Hormuz in surprise talks held in New York under the mediation of Qatar between Tehran’s foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, and Donald Trump’s envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.

    Trump said the three-hour talks held in a room at the UN headquarters had gone very well and been very productive. He suggested further talks were possible imminently, which led to the price of a barrel of Brent crude to fall to below $100 (£75) for the first time in two weeks. Witkoff said the talks had been “encouraging, constructive and successful”.

title: The climate fight has one great ally. You just can’t look at it directly | Bill McKibben
content:
There is hope in solar power. As the UN meets, we are urging leaders to pursue a clear goal: clean energy for all by 2030

  • Our message to global leaders: we need solar power everywhere by the decade’s end

    • Our message to global leaders: we need solar power everywhere by the decade’s end

    As climate experts from around the world gather in New York for their annual week of talking through the world’s deepest dilemma, the vibes are mostly bad.

    Though 2026 seems likely to set a new global temperature record (and 2027, as El Niño gathers steam, is almost certain to break it), and though the planet has careened from one climate disaster to another (European heatwaves that killed tens of thousands, a Nepali flood that wiped out entire communities), and though scientists warn that we’re reaching precisely the global tipping points they’ve long feared (the new research on the faltering great currents of the Atlantic should send a literal chill up your spine), there’s a distinct lack of political momentum.

    The path forward is difficult, but the way is clear. We want solar for everyone, everywhere, before the decade is out.
snippet: There is hope in solar power. As the UN meets, we are urging leaders to pursue a clear goal: clean energy for all by 2030

title: Fears mount that next UN chief will downgrade climate action
content:
Experts say some of António Guterres’s possible successors could be ‘disastrous’ for efforts to tackle crisis

Fears are mounting that the next UN secretary general will downgrade the priority of the climate crisis, according to climate and civil society experts.

The current secretary general, António Guterres, has been the most forthright on the subject, calling fossil fuel companies “the godfathers of climate chaos” and warning governments they are rushing down a “highway to hell” by failing to cut greenhouse gas emissions.
